review_notes:
I read the whole file but did not open any related sources. I checked each declaration for a useful, low-cost generalisation.

The general section is already stated for arbitrary topological spaces X and Y. It uses T2Space only where the proof needs a closed embedding of the compact solid torus.

The Euclidean helper lemmas (`tangentVector`, `continuous_tangentVector`, `exists_forall_notMem_span_tangentVector`) are already stated for a general real inner product space V. The dimension hypothesis is `2 < finrank`, which also handles the degenerate dimensions. The `ℝ³` specialisation in `exists_normalFrame`, `exists_normalDisc` and the main theorem is needed because the construction uses the cross product, which exists only in dimension three.

The assumptions of the main theorem are C², immersion and injectivity. These match what the tubular neighbourhood theorem and the density argument need.

The only generalisation I considered was replacing `[T2Space X]` in `frontier_image` and `exteriorFrontierHomeomorph` by a closed-range hypothesis. I judged it marginal, because it would help only in non-Hausdorff ambient spaces and would complicate the statement. I did not report it.
